alignments.note: Postpositive δέ takes the ASV's clause-initial *but*.
Dative pronoun with its case preposition riding along under rule 21's determinerless clause; headed on *them*.

The article governing κλητοῖς realizes nothing: αὐτοῖς has already written the antecedent *them*, so no determiner and no antecedent pronoun is left for it. This is rule 20's stated contrast, `Ὑμῖν … τοῖς ἔθνεσιν` → *to you that are Gentiles*, and rule 92 keeps the supplied relativizer and copula on the expressed complement rather than on the article.
The substantival adjective recast as a finite relative clause takes *that are called* whole, the relativizer and copula being rule 7 and 9 helpers on it (rule 92); headed on the lexical *called*.
τε … καί is spelled out with two English words, so each particle keeps its own: *both* to τε under rule 70.
The second of the two written conjunctions belongs to καί under rule 70.
Anarthrous δύναμιν with a supplied *the*: no article competes, so the determiner is an ordinary rule 7 helper on the noun (rule 51's anarthrous clause), headed on *power*.

Genitive noun rendered *of + noun*; the case preposition rides with it under rule 21's determinerless clause and rule 17 heads it on *God*. The ASV reverses the Greek order θεοῦ δύναμιν without crossing the nouns' senses.
Anarthrous σοφίαν with a supplied *the*, analysed exactly as δύναμιν above under rule 24; headed on *wisdom*.
Second genitive θεοῦ with its case preposition, headed on *God*, as with the first.

review_notes: τοῖς κλητοῖς: the competing reading gives the article the supplied relativizer under rule 31's verbless-modifier carve-out. That carve-out names a prepositional phrase or a bare adverb, and here αὐτοῖς has already spelled the antecedent, which is precisely rule 20's `Ὑμῖν … τοῖς ἔθνεσιν` case; so the article is left unrepresented and the adjective keeps *that are called*.
τε and καί each receive one of the two written English conjunctions (rule 70's spelled-out arm), rather than joining *both … and* into one unit.
The two θεοῦ / accusative-noun pairs are analysed alike under rule 24, each supplied *the* staying with its anarthrous noun and each *of* with its genitive.
